 SCCH-1 2 MVC No.1534/2020  JUDGMENT

The Petitioner being owner of the car No. KA-53-MB- 4456 filed petition under Sec.166 of I.M.V. Act claiming damages worth of Rs.15,00,000/- from the respondents who are the owner and insurer of C.M. Radhakrishna vs Krishnaiah on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51451352/
1 the lorry No.MH-05-2727 alleging that on 06.07.2019 at 1.00 PM when driver of the car No.KA-53-MB-4456 driving the car on Kolar-Bengaluru road, NH-75, near Ramasandra gate driver of a lorry No. MH-05-2727 negligently without furnishing signal suddenly stopped the lorry on the middle of the road thereby made the car to dash to the rear part of the lorry resulting in the damage to the car.
2.
Regarding the accident Vemagal Police registered a case in Cr. No.121/2019 with respect to the incident.
Petitioner has spent Rs.8,50,000/- to get repair the car.

3. In response to the notice, the respondent No.1 & 2 appeared through their respective Advocates and filed written statements separately denying the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident and quantum of the damages suffered by the petitioner.

4. On the basis of the pleadings on 03.03.2021 this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that an accident has occurred on 06.07.2019 at about 01.00 p.m. on Bangalore-Kolar Road, Near Ramasandra Gate, within the jurisdiction of Vemagal police station rash and negligent driving of the Lorry bearing Registration No.MH-05-2727 by its driver when the petitioner was travelling in the car bearing Reg.No.KA-53-MB-4456 and in the said accident, petitioners car bearing Reg. No.KA-53-MB-4456 suffered damages?
2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order?
5. On 03.03.2023, 25.03.2023, 24.05.2023 petitioner deposed as PW.1 and produced 8 documents at Exhibits P.1 to P.8.
On 20.07.2023, 21.08.2023, 07.09.2023, petitioner produced evidence of Officer of the United Insurance Company and Body Shape Advisor as PW.2 and 3 and get produced 5 documents at Ex.P9 to P13.

On 04.01.2024 respondent No.2 insurance company produced evidence of Officer of Insurance company as RW.1 and get produced copy of the insurance policy at Ex.R.1.
6.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of both the parties and perused the records.

7. On the basis of the materials placed on record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ...

Due to the negligent use of the car No. KA-53-MB-4456 and Lorry No.
MH- 05-2727 at the ratio of 50:50 the accident taken place resulting in the damage to the car, Issue No.2 ...
Petitioner is entitle to receive Rs.1,00,000/- with current and future interest @ 6% p.a. as damages from respondents, Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
C.M. Radhakrishna vs Krishnaiah on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51451352/
2 REASONS 8.

sentences.text: Issue No.1:-

In the evidence affidavit, petitioner/PW.1 stated that on 06.07.2019 at 1.00 PM when driver of the car No.KA-53-MB-4456 drove the car on Kolar-Bengaluru road, NH-75, near Ramasandra gate driver of the lorry No.MH-05-2727 which was running in the same direction negligently without furnishing signal suddenly stopped the lorry on the middle of the road thereby made car to dash to the rear part of the lorry and caused damage to the car, resulting in the damages to petitioner.
In the written statement, respondents denied the allegation asserting that due to the negligence driving of the car the incident taken place.
9. In the cross-examination PW.1 stated that during accident three persons are in the car and he is not present in the car.
In the evidence PW.2, PW.3, RW.1 stated nothing regarding the reason and mode of the accident.

10. Ex.P1 is the copy of the FIR and complaint pertaining to Crime No.121/2019 of Vemagal Police Station registered on 07.07.2019 at 2.30 PM against the driver of the lorry No. MH-05-2727 for having committed the offence punishable under Section 279, 337 of IPC., regarding the collision taken place between front part of the car No. KA- 53-MB-4456 and rear part of the lorry bearing No.
MH-05- 2727 on the basis of the complaint presented by Sevanth R S/o Ramakrishna.
11. Ex.P2 is the copy of the spot mahazar recorded on 07.07.2019.
Ex.P3 is the copy of the Motor Vehicle Accident Report dated 18.07.2019.

Ex.P4 is the copy of the chargesheet filed by Vemagal Police in Crime No. 121/2019 against Manjunatha S/o Govindaraju, driver of the lorry No.
MH-05-2727 for having committed the offences punishable under Sec. 279, 337, 338 IPC.
In the photos the damage suffered by the car No. KA-53-MB-4456 are visible.
12. In the file, the evidence of the eye witnesses of the incident are not available.
In this case, at this stage there are no reasons to disbelieve the contents of the police records regarding the reason and mode of the accident.

Hence, I have concluded that on 06.07.2019 at 1.00 PM on Kolar-Bengaluru NH-75 near Ramasandra Gate, in view of the negligent use of the car No.KA-53-MB-4456 and lorry No. MH-05-2727 at the ratio of 50:50 collision taken place between front part of car and rear part of lorry resulting in the damage to the car.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 accordingly.
13. Issue No.2:

In the petition and evidence affidavit petitioner stated that in the accident the car was fully damaged, which was towed to Shahwar Motives Pvt., Ltd., Jayamahal Extension,
Bengaluru who issued estimation worth of Rs.8,50,000/- to repair the car.

Petitioner stated that he has spent Rs.50,000/- for towing and in view of the damage suffered to the car spent Rs.1,00,000/-
for personal conveyance.
14. In the written statement respondents denied the allegation regarding the quantum of the damages suffered by the petitioner.

15. In the cross-examination petitioner stated that his car had policy issued by United India Insurance Company and he has not claimed damages from the insurer of his car and stated C.M. Radhakrishna vs Krishnaiah on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51451352/
3 non-filing of the complaint before Consumer Forum alleging non-providing of the damages by the insurer of his car.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: PW.1 stated
that insurer of car conducted survey
. PW.1 stated that he did not get repaired the car.

16. In the evidence PW2 Officer of the United India Insurance Company produced Survey Report,
repudiation letter at Ex.P10 & P11.

In the cross-examination PW.2 stated United India Insurance Company issued comprehensive policy with respect to car No.KA-53-MB- 4456 get surveyed the damages suffered to the car and stated about issuance of Repudiation Letter marked and Ex.P11 due to the violation of the driver clause of the policy.
17. In the evidence PW.3 stated that the car No. KA- 53-MB-4456 was towed to the showroom and a mechanic assessed damage and estimated cost of the repair of the car at Rs.8,34,006/-.
In the cross-examination PW.3 admitted that in Ex.P5 estimation nothing has been mentioned about the rates of the spare parts.
PW.3 admitted that in Ex.P6 the damage caused to the parts of the car is not mentioned.
PW.3 stated that car No. KA-53- MB-4456 was manufactured in the year 2014.
18. In the evidence RW.1 the officer of the respondent No.2 insurance company reiterated the same defence as narrated in the written statement.
In the cross- examination RW.1 admitted that in the chargesheet nothing has been mentioned to show that the driver of the car had no licence to drive the car.
19. In the copy of the RC pertaining to car No. KA-53- MB-4456 name of the petitioner is noted as the registered owner and registration date is noted as 26.04.2014.

Ex.P5 is copy of the estimation regarding the spare parts and labour charges to repair the car No.KA-53-MB-4456 in which cost of the spare parts and labour charges are noted at Rs.6,36,995/- and Rs.1,57,011/- respectively.
In the photos the damage suffered by right front part of the car are visible.

Ex.P11 shows that on the allegation of violation of the terms of the driver clause of the policy, the United India Insurance Company the insurer of the car No. KA-53- MB-4456 repudiated the claim made by the petitioner own damage claim.

20. As referred above, in the evidence petitioner admitted that he did not get repair the car till the date of his evidence and after lapse of approximately 5 years from the date of registration of the car the accident taken place resulting in the damage to the car.
Hence, I have estimated the damages suffered by the car No. KA-53-MB-4456 in the accident dated 06.07.2019 at Rs.2,00,000/-.
In view of the finding recorded on the Issue No.1, I came to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitled to receive Rs.1,00,000/- with current and future interest @ 6% p.a., as damages.
Copy of the policy marked at Ex.R1 shows that as on the date of accident lorry No. MH-05-2727 had insurance coverage with respondent No.2.
In the file, there are no evidence to show contravention of any terms of policy by respondent No.1 owner of the lorry No. MH-05- 2727.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being owner and insurer of the lorry No. MH- 05-2727 are liable to pay Rs.1,00,000/- with current and future interest @ 6% p.a., to the petitioner towards damages.

Hence, I answer Issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed.
